newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke says no intention to put VAT on food.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke says no intention to put VAT on food.

text.p: UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke denied on Thursday claims by the opposition Labour party that the government intended to put value-added tax on food if it wins the next election.
"I am not contemplating VAT on food," Clarke told BBC's Radio Four.
Labour is running a campaign saying VAT on food will be one of the Conservatives' "first targets" if it wins the election, which must be held by May.
Clarke said he had been working hard to get Britain's economic fundamentals right.
"As soon as I can, I'll get back to a tax-cutting agenda. That's what I'm doing," he said.

When asked about Europe, he reiterated the Conservatives "wait-and-see" policy. My intention is to remain involved...in the negotiations, wati-and see..and then decide what is in the British interest," he said.
"We have the healthiest economic recovery in Europe, we're doing very well there...and it'll be some time before we're in any position to decide what's in the interest of UK limited."
